item.title: IMPROMPTU LI - Doozie Doe Run (24 R) — Fri Jul 24, 8:00 AM
item.description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup Ride Leader: Bruce Black
An enjoyable ride from Lititz exploring the Speedwell Forge area before heading to Manheim for some coffee at Today's Grind Coffee Shop. The pace will be 14 - 16 mph average with multiple regroup points (like 4 or 5). Please park in the upper parking lot of the library.
This ride is a social ride, but cyclists are not expected to stay in one group. Cyclists may pedal at their own comfortable paces. Please be supportive of the other cyclists to avoid anyone biking alone or being dropped off the back of the last group.

item.title: Anti-Fascist Craft Night in Lititz with the Warwick Democrats! — Wed Aug 5, 3:00 PM — Lititz
item.description:
We love democracy. We love crafts. We love snacks. And we love civic engagement. You too? Join us for **Anti-Fascist Craft Night** in Lititz—a low-key hang where we cut up cereal boxes and old magazines, make wild collage postcards and letters, and send our thoughts (and shade) to our elected officials. Make your voice heard in a weirdly therapeutic and hands-on way! **What to bring:** * Clean cardboard (cereal/snack boxes) or card stock * Old magazines, catalogs, newspapers, greeting cards, etc

item.description:
Enjoy a little ‘staycation’ with Allegro as we close our 25th season! For this finale, we’re going around the world and back in 80 minutes! We’ll go with Rossini to Algiers, spend some time with Faure in France, take a tour through Italy with Mendelssohn, and return to the states for Brian Norcross’s new piece ‘Dogwood.’

item.title: Medicare Open Enrollment — Tue Oct 20, 11:00 AM — Quarryville
item.description:
Health & Wellness, Seniors
Medicare Annual Open Enrollment Appointments at Quarryville LibraryLancaster County Office of Aging runs a program called PA Medi, formerly APPRISE. This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round. They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026. Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc. If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything. item.description:

Who may naturalize, and can you pass the civics test??This event is offered solely as information about the American legal system and should not be construed as legal advice. If you need legal counsel on this or other immigration matters, please consult a qualified immigration attorney.

item.title: Valley Forge Park River Trail (Pawlings Rd) — Sun Jul 26, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Walking Tails Directions: From the intersection of Egypt Road and Park Ave./Pawlings Road, proceed on Pawlings Road heading towards the Schuylkill River. You will pass Mill Grove on your right, St. Gabriel Hall on your left and Pawling Farm on your left. You are getting close when you pass Sullivan Blvd. on your left and Gertrude St. on your right. You turn left on the next and last left (right before you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River). Look for the River Trail Valley Forge Park sign visible from Pawlings Road. The gravel parking lot is straight ahead and also visible from Pawlings Road. If you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River, you have gone too far and are now in Chester county.
CLICK DIRECTLY ON THE MAP IF YOU THINK YOU ARE LOST. IT WILL BRING YOU RIGHT TO US WHERE WE MEET.
This walk goes out about 1.5 miles along the Schuylkill River and then we come back the way we came, for a total of 3 miles. This is a dirt/gravel/mulch trail through the woods.

item.title: Patriarchy, Matriarchy & Democracy: A Two-Part Online Discussion — Thu Aug 13, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Freethought Society This is an LFS online discussion series, held on Google Meet. Across two sessions, we’ll explore how patriarchy and matriarchy organize power, care, law, family, sex, money, violence, and democracy. We’ll use consciousness-raising style discussion rules: speak personally, listen carefully, don’t interrupt, and don’t debate someone while they are speaking. For each question, we’ll do a speaking round first. After everyone who wants to speak has spoken, Susan will offer brief evidence, examples, or definitions to deepen the discussion. **Part 1**
* What is patriarchy? * What is matriarchy? * How do these systems operate?
**Part 2**
* What are the benefits of each? * What are the dangers or pitfalls of each? * Can democracy exist inside a patriarchy?
This is not a lecture. It is a structured conversation about power, equality, family, sex, law, care, violence, democracy, and what kind of world we want to build.
Source: Meetup: Lancaster Freethought Socie
